narrative.overview: LearnUp reads like an institution's own record-keeping desk, not a generic SaaS admin panel. Every surface should feel like it belongs to a place where things are tracked precisely and nothing disappears quietly: the Supervisor's screens have the warm, grounded confidence of a registrar's office (sand, terracotta, deep sage), while the Estudiante and Profesor share a cooler, more scholarly blue -- two rooms in the same building, never two different products stitched together. The system is deliberately role-split rather than single-primary: Supervisor surfaces run on the sage/terracotta/sand palette, Estudiante and Profesor surfaces run on the scholar-blue/celeste palette. Components are tactile and confident: buttons give real press feedback, cards lift gently on hover, nothing animates just to animate. The explicit anti-reference is the generic 'made by AI' look -- oversaturated gradients, decorative emoji, interchangeable stock icons, surfaces that are too smooth to feel like they belong to a real institution.
keyCharacteristics: Two deliberate accent worlds (warm for Supervisor, cool for Estudiante/Profesor), never mixed on the same screen.
Flat-by-default surfaces with a single soft shadow-sm, stepping up only on hover or in overlays.
Rounded-corner, border-first cards -- a 1px neutral border does the separating before any shadow.
Every interactive element gives tactile press/hover feedback; nothing is inert.
Icons are a single hand-picked Heroicons-outline set (1.5px stroke) -- never mixed families, never emoji.

rules.name: The Role-Split Palette Rule
rules.body: Supervisor screens never use Scholar Blue/Ocean Deep/Celeste; Estudiante and Profesor screens never use Sage/Terracotta/Sand. A shared component switches its whole token set by role, it never blends the two.

rules.name: The One Warm Signal Rule
rules.body: Terracotta (either side's secondary accent) is reserved for things the user must notice once and act on -- a temporary password, a pending first login, an archived state -- never for routine decoration.

rules.name: The No-Caption-Smaller-Than-12px Rule
rules.body: text-xs is the floor for anything read as a sentence (badges/eyebrows only); card detail lines use text-sm so they stay comfortable at a glance.

rules.name: The Depth-Is-a-Response Rule
rules.body: Nothing above shadow-sm appears at rest. A heavier shadow always means the element is reacting to you (hover) or floating above everything else (modal/overlay), never decoration.

dos: Do keep each screen entirely inside its role's palette -- check which esAdmin/role flag a shared component branches on before adding a color.
Do give every clickable element a press state (active:scale-[0.97]) and every hoverable card a lift, even on small/secondary buttons.
Do use plain hyphens (-) for any separator in UI copy -- never an em dash or middle dot.
Do reserve Terracotta/Ocean-Deep (the secondary accent) for things the user must notice once, not routine UI chrome.
donts: Don't mix Sage/Terracotta/Sand with Scholar-Blue/Ocean-Deep/Celeste on the same screen, even in a shared component.
Don't add a shadow heavier than shadow-sm to anything at rest; depth is earned by hover or overlay status only.

Don't reach for gradients, emoji, or generic stock icon packs -- the explicit anti-reference is the 'looks AI-generated' look. Every icon comes from the project's single hand-picked Heroicons-outline set.
Don't drop below text-sm for anything meant to be read as a sentence; text-xs is for badges and eyebrows only.
